buckets.name: Book repair / diagnostic visit
buckets.definition: Customer reports a non-emergency equipment or plumbing problem and wants a technician scheduled.
buckets.includes: Burning smell from vents, AC blowing warm or not cooling, furnace won't turn on, blank thermostat, grinding noise, water pooling at indoor unit, backed-up kitchen sink, water heater pilot going out. Also covers waitlist requests and questions about whether the maintenance plan would lower the cost of this repair.
buckets.excludes: Gas, CO or sparks emergencies. Warranty-coverage questions on failed equipment. Annual tune-ups.

buckets.name: Book annual tune-up
buckets.definition: Customer wants to schedule routine annual HVAC maintenance.
buckets.includes: Annual tune-up scheduling, including waitlist requests.

buckets.name: Manage existing appointment
buckets.definition: Customer is calling about an appointment that is already booked.
buckets.includes: Reschedules, cancellations because the issue was already fixed, confirming an appointment window, and technician no-shows (window passed with no arrival or call).

buckets.name: Billing & payments
buckets.definition: Routine account balance, payment, or charge-explanation requests that are not disputes.
buckets.includes: Balance lookups, paying an invoice (via a texted secure link), explaining an unrecognized invoice and emailing an itemized copy, and suspected double charges.
buckets.excludes: Disputes over quoted vs. invoiced price. Refund demands. Membership autopay.

buckets.name: Membership (Comfort Club)
buckets.definition: Questions or account changes about the maintenance membership.
buckets.includes: Plan info and price (including the $149 check), renewal charge timing, cancelling membership, autopay setup, upgrading to Plus, and member discount on a new system.
buckets.excludes: Questions about whether the plan would save money on a repair being booked; those go to the repair bucket.

buckets.name: Warranty questions & claims
buckets.definition: Questions about warranty coverage, registration, transfer, or filing a claim.
buckets.includes: Warranty claims on last year's install, compressor coverage (often followed by booking a repair), labor warranty on a repeat blower failure, manufacturer registration status, and warranty transfer to a new homeowner.
buckets.excludes: Generic repairs with no warranty question.

buckets.name: Residential replacement estimate
buckets.definition: Customer wants a ballpark cost for replacing an aging home system and/or a free in-home estimate.
buckets.includes: Replacement of an 18-year-old system, ballpark price, and booking a comfort advisor visit.

buckets.name: Complaints, disputes & refunds
buckets.definition: Customer is dissatisfied and needs human or manager resolution.
buckets.includes: Invoice higher than the quote (after-hours, disposal or permit fees), refund for a failed repair, disputed $4,000 replacement recommendation, rude technician, and repeated unreturned calls.
buckets.excludes: Neutral invoice questions or double-charge checks.

buckets.name: Safety emergency
buckets.definition: Potentially hazardous situation needing immediate safety guidance and dispatch.
buckets.includes: Gas smell, carbon monoxide alarm, sparks from the outdoor unit.
buckets.excludes: Burning smell from vents, which these lines treat as a routine booking.

buckets.name: Non-service / out of scope
buckets.definition: Calls not about residential service for an existing or prospective customer.
buckets.includes: Job/hiring inquiries, wrong number (Meridian Dental), and commercial rooftop replacement quotes.

notes: Counts are approximate. 1) Burning smell from vents is bucketed as a routine repair because every one of these calls was booked normally; decide whether policy should treat it as a safety emergency. 2) Technician no-shows are placed in appointment management, though one asked for a fee waiver and could count as a complaint. 3) Compressor-warranty and repeat-blower calls usually end in a booking; they are classified by the opening warranty question. 4) Membership autopay could go under billing instead; it is placed under membership. 5) Commercial quotes are grouped with out-of-scope; split them out if commercial is a real line of business. 6) Several lines mention a 'Trane' or 'Goodman' unit on kitchen-sink calls, which suggests transcript or summary noise. 7) All complaints and safety calls ended in a callback or escalation, while most other buckets resolved on the call. That points to the first seven buckets as the AI-automatable set, though registration, warranty transfer, and replacement-estimate calls sometimes needed callbacks.
